qt_scombat_requires_sights: Use only if the GM uses the sighted/unsighted split. Confirm the target and equipment before choosing this shooting method.
qt_scombat_requires_cover: Use this optional cover model instead of the Basic Set coverage penalty, not in addition to it.
qt_scombat_requires_rangefinding: Requires a valid measured range or range card, compatible adjustable sights, and an aimed shot.
qt_scombat_requires_obscuration: The GM selects the amount of affected line of sight. Assess physical cover separately.
qt_scombat_requires_wind: Use the optional wind model for a crosswind on long-range shots, not front or rear wind.
qt_scombat_requires_maneuvers: Requires optional Martial Arts maneuvers or combat options; use a ready melee attack as appropriate.
qt_scombat_requires_grips: Confirm a compatible weapon, grip, hands available, and Ready to change grip before using the modifiers.
qt_scombat_requires_step: Requires the optional alternatives to Retreat in melee and a legal free space to step into.
qt_scombat_requires_bleeding: Requires optional Basic Set bleeding and the GM’s Severe Bleeding option. Enter a qualifying wound, not raw damage.
qt_scombat_requires_bad: Requires a GM-selected Basic Abstract Difficulty (BAD) for the phase. Use it to replace detailed situational modifiers or to rate an abstract henchman, never both.
qt_scombat_requires_chases: Use the abstract Action 2 chase subsystem. Do not add these bands to the Basic Set shooting penalty or apply BAD to chase rolls.
qt_scombat_sight_gear_mask: Gas mask, dive mask or similar
qt_scombat_sight_gear_weapon_night_sight: Looking through a weapon’s night sight
qt_scombat_target_not_visible: Target not visible; GM must judge location
qt_scombat_sights_no_sighted: Firing from the hip or wearing NVGs precludes sighted and aimed shooting.
qt_scombat_sights_no_weapon_night_sight: Using a weapon’s night sight requires looking through it. Select sighted or aimed shooting to benefit from it.
qt_scombat_sights_no_visibility: No numeric sight adjustment here: resolve an unseen target under visibility and known-location rules first.
qt_scombat_sights_unsighted: Uses Attack or Move and Attack, not Aim or All-Out Attack (Determined). It permits Dodge where otherwise available.
qt_scombat_sights_sighted: Uses All-Out Attack (Determined): +1 to Guns from the maneuver, with no active defense.
qt_scombat_sights_aimed: Uses Aim followed by All-Out Attack (Determined). Benefits of Aim and the maneuver are separate from these visibility and equipment adjustments.
qt_scombat_sights_scope: The close unsighted adjustment covers only one point of darkness. Enter darkness after deciding how the optics affect it; technique buy-offs, equipment bonuses and target identification are not calculated.
qt_scombat_braced_and_aimed: Weapon braced against cover and aimed
qt_scombat_cover_pair: Shot around cover against the exposed target: {incoming:+d}. Shot back from that cover: {outgoing:+d}.
qt_scombat_cover_scope: Bracing and aiming remove this model’s outgoing penalty for medium/heavy cover; normal Aim benefits are separate. For shooting through cover, also resolve the covered hit location and cover DR.
qt_scombat_range_source_near_landmark: Target within 1 yard of a plotted landmark
qt_scombat_sights_set: Sights adjusted to exploit known range
qt_scombat_rangefinding_set_sights: Set the sights to claim the full bonus: normally Ready, with exceptions for appropriate traits or auto-adjusting sights.
qt_scombat_rangefinding_scope: Use a valid plotted landmark or instrument. If a scope is used, the full rangefinding bonus increases its Acc bonus; this lookup does not resolve every Aim cap.
qt_scombat_obscuration: Impairment along the line of sight
qt_scombat_chosen_increment: Base increment chosen by the GM (optional)
qt_scombat_increment_at_most: Choose a positive increment no greater than {high}.
qt_scombat_increment_select: Enter the chosen increment to obtain a Vision modifier.
qt_scombat_increment_result: Vision modifier: {modifier:+d}, using one step per {effective}.
qt_scombat_increment_shelter: Heavy vegetation doubles the precipitation increment, not the vegetation’s own interval.
qt_scombat_increment_scope: This is a Vision adjustment, not cover DR. For a shot at a target whose position is known to within one yard, this supplement caps the obscuration penalty at −4; check the Basic Set visibility rule as well.
qt_scombat_invalid_increment: The chosen increment is outside this condition’s supported interval.
qt_scombat_crosswind_result: Wind adjustment: {modifier:+d} (range steps past {threshold}: {steps}; wind {wind:+d}; correction {correction:+d}).
qt_scombat_crosswind_scope: Each successful Precision Aiming roll cancels up to two points of wind penalty, never granting a positive wind bonus.
qt_scombat_scale_strong: GM allows scaling Strong per two dice
qt_scombat_maneuver_not_ready: This maneuver requires a ready melee attack.
qt_scombat_maneuver_telegraphic: +4 to hit; the target gets +2 to active defenses. Determine critical-hit range using the skill before +4.
qt_scombat_maneuver_telegraphic_limits: Do not combine with Deceptive Attack, Riposte, an earlier Feint, or the Evaluate bonus.
qt_scombat_maneuver_defensive: Defensive Attack: damage adjustment {damage:+d}; one step. Target gets +1 to defend against a grab or grapple.
qt_scombat_maneuver_defensive_limits: Choose the defense benefit before attacking. Balance, the weapon you used and kicking determine which benefit is legal; consult the maneuver details.
qt_scombat_maneuver_committed: Committed Attack: {hit:+d} to hit, {damage:+d} damage, movement of up to {steps} step(s).
qt_scombat_maneuver_committed_limits: No retreat. No Parry with the attacking hand(s), no Block with a shield used to attack, and no Dodge after a kick; other active defenses are at −2.
qt_scombat_martial_grip_defensive_two: Defensive Grip, two-handed or versatile weapon
qt_scombat_side_attack: Parrying an attack from the side
qt_scombat_grip_result: Grip modifiers only: attack {attack:+d}, damage {damage:+d}, Parry {parry:+d}.
qt_scombat_grip_reversed_scope: This covers ordinary weapon attacks and weapon Parry only. Check Reach, attack direction and special unarmed/tonfa parries separately.
qt_scombat_grip_defensive_scope: This grip takes two hands. These modifiers do not include the usual side-attack penalty, the special tip grip, or Wild Swing and breakage effects.
qt_scombat_standing_and_space: Standing, with a legal adjacent space
qt_scombat_mobile_defense: Defense would get +3 instead of +1 when retreating
qt_scombat_slip_unavailable: This option requires a standing defender and a legal step.
qt_scombat_slip_result: Net movement modifier to active defense against this opponent: {modifier:+d}.
qt_scombat_slip_side_scope: Step sideways into an adjacent space that keeps the same distance from the attacker.
qt_scombat_slip_toward_scope: Step toward the attacker into a legal adjacent space. Stop Thrust adds a further −1.
qt_scombat_slip_scope: Apply restrictions that prevent an active defense or a retreat separately. This card does not move tokens or validate a map path.
qt_scombat_bleeding_injury: Injury after DR and wounding rules (HP)
qt_scombat_bleed_no_injury: No injury to use in the bleeding lookup.
qt_scombat_bleed_artery_ineligible: This damage type does not qualify for a direct strike on a vein or artery under these rules.
qt_scombat_bleed_result: Bleeding HT modifier: {modifier:+d} every {seconds} s (injury size {size:+d}, severe effect {extra:+d}).
qt_scombat_bleed_surgery_scope: With the severe wound treatment option, stopping this bleed requires Surgery at the same modifier, not ordinary First Aid.
qt_scombat_bleed_first_aid_scope: If the GM uses severe bandaging, apply the total bleeding modifier to the First Aid roll to stop this bleed.
qt_scombat_bleed_scope: Single wound only. Revert dismemberment to ordinary bleeding once blood loss equals the crippling threshold; use the book and GM judgment for combined wounds.
qt_scombat_bleed_lasting_scope: For major wounds here, the separate optional lasting-injury tables and subsequent HT recovery checks require GM adjudication.
qt_scombat_bad_method_enemy: Derive from Enemy’s basic point value
qt_scombat_personal_adjustments: Personal or gear modifiers brought by the PC
qt_scombat_bad_npc_alternative: Use BAD for henchman skill instead
qt_scombat_bad_not_applied: No BAD adjustment to the PC’s skill in this situation.
qt_scombat_bad_scope: BAD replaces detailed situational difficulty; do not also lower the PC’s skill when using the abstract henchman-skill alternative. Do not apply it to attacks, chase rolls or ordinary complementary-skill rolls.
qt_scombat_chase_method: How the current band is set
qt_scombat_chase_result: Current band: {band}. Ranged attack distance modifier within the chase: {modifier:+d}.
qt_scombat_chase_both_static: With two static maneuvers, the range does not change this round.
qt_scombat_chase_one_static: The moving side can shift once regardless of the contest: up to two shifts if it wins by 5–9, or three if it wins by 10 or more. The static side receives no speed bonus.
qt_scombat_chase_steps: The winner may shift the distance band by up to {steps} step(s) when neither side is static.
qt_scombat_chase_scope: Round duration is abstract. Use the actual starting distance only to pick the initial band. The quarry can escape by shifting beyond Extreme; special maneuvers and direction choices are adjudicated separately.
qt_explore_hearing_deaf: Hearing rolls are unavailable with Deafness.
qt_explore_sense_target: Target number: {target} (base {base}, Acute Sense {acute:+d}, remaining adjustments {modifier:+d}).
qt_explore_hearing_notes: Between distance bands, this table uses the farther band. Hearing does not decode speech; the GM may ask for comprehension or a Quick Contest against Stealth.
qt_explore_invalid_hearing_distance: Enter a positive distance to the sound.
qt_explore_vision_task_other: Vision-based skill, attack or later interpretation
qt_explore_actively_watching: Actively looking in the right direction
qt_explore_located_target: Target already found with a Vision roll
qt_explore_vision_unavailable: No usable vision (e.g. total darkness without an aid)
qt_explore_vision_no_roll: No Vision roll is possible under the selected conditions.
qt_explore_vision_notes: For ordinary targets, plain sight allows only size and distance adjustments and excludes concealment. An exposed light source aimed within the observer’s view can also qualify. In total darkness, unaided Vision is impossible.
qt_explore_sense_comprehension: Noticing is separate from interpreting. Use IQ for general comprehension or the appropriate skill for specialist knowledge.
qt_explore_taste_smell_trait_discriminat: Discriminatory Smell or Taste, as applicable
qt_explore_taste_smell_unavailable: {sense} rolls are unavailable with the selected disadvantage.
qt_explore_taste_smell_notes: The GM sets adjustments for intensity or masking. This lookup does not infer a scent’s strength, range, or identity.
qt_explore_horizon_plain: A deliberate signal in plain sight gives +10 to the active Vision roll.
qt_explore_horizon_light: Darkness becomes a bonus of {bonus:+d} to see this light signal.
qt_explore_horizon_notes: Use height above ground (including elevation), not the observer’s or target’s silhouette. This Earth-like horizon does not check obstacles or guarantee detection.
qt_explore_invalid_horizon_size: Choose a height modifier from −10 through +30.
qt_explore_track_conditions: Conditions on loose snow or sand
qt_explore_track_loose_calm: Loose snow/sand, no wind or wash
qt_explore_track_loose_wind_water: Loose snow/sand, strong wind or wash
qt_explore_terrain_foraging_note: Roll only the dice subtotal here. The resulting modifier is for a separate foraging check, not a yield in meals.
qt_explore_terrain_underwater: Underwater profiles assume the party can travel underwater. This lookup gives no underwater tracking or travel modifier.
qt_explore_terrain_tracking_condition_ig: The selected wind or wash adjustment applies only to Arctic, desert, or beach profiles.
qt_explore_terrain_mixed: For mixed terrain, use the dominant profile rather than stacking factors; eligible Survival specialties can still apply.
qt_explore_invalid_foraging_roll: The raw dice subtotal does not match this terrain’s dice.
qt_explore_invalid_terrain_surface: The ski and skate presets here apply only to Arctic terrain.
qt_explore_hiking_success: Successful Hiking or substitute skill roll
qt_explore_hiking_full_day: The standard daily estimate uses the entire day, including preparation and rest.
qt_explore_hiking_move_note: Use Move after encumbrance, injury and fatigue. Apply only weather effects not already included in the terrain factor.
qt_explore_hiking_fatigue_note: If you stop for another action, the GM assesses road-march fatigue, including load and heat (p. 426).
qt_explore_invalid_hiking_hours: Foraging hours cannot exceed the marching time of the selected model.
qt_explore_climb_no_roll: An ordinary ladder needs no Climbing roll.
qt_explore_climb_roll_note: Roll at the start and every five minutes. Climbing defaults to DX−5; the GM handles falls and safety gear.
qt_explore_climb_fatigue_note: Combat climbing requires Move and costs at least 1 FP; use twice any higher normal cost assigned by the GM.
qt_explore_swim_speed: Water speed after encumbrance: {speed}; distance in 10 seconds: {distance}.
qt_explore_swim_aquatic: Amphibious and Aquatic characters do not need the deep-water survival roll.
qt_explore_swim_check_note: Roll on entry and every five minutes. Swimming defaults to HT−4; on a failed roll, lose 1 FP and retry after five seconds.
qt_explore_swim_fatigue: Check fatigue every {minutes} min against the better of HT or Swimming. Failure costs 1 FP. Low FP reduces Move separately.

gm_dice_error_invalid_expression: Invalid expression. Use count d sides, with an optional modifier: 104d6+20 or 3d-1.
gm_dice_error_dice_count: Use between 1 and 10,000,000 dice per roll.
gm_dice_error_dice_sides: Use between 1 and 1,000,000 sides per die.
gm_dice_error_dice_modifier: The modifier must be an integer between -1,000,000,000 and +1,000,000,000.

engine_error_mobile_encounter_strategy: In the first encounter round, a mobile force cannot retreat and may only use Mobile Defense as a defense.
engine_error_invalid_encounter_strategy: Encounter battles disallow Deliberate Attack and Deliberate Defense.
engine_error_invalid_defense_bonus: Invalid Defense Bonus: use a nonnegative integer.

ui_help_text:
1. Choose a tool from the sidebar or Home. Use ★ to keep favorites.

2. Search for equipment or abilities. Filters do not replace the active item: confirm with Use in calculation. Full record shows available fields, not rule certification.

3. Fill in the fields. Red messages indicate invalid numbers. Empty optional fields use calculator defaults. Rule-specific combinations are still checked by the engine.

4. Calculate does not roll dice. Roll/Resolve may generate random results. Editing inputs makes the previous result outdated.

5. Apply to session confirms combat changes; review the preview and use Undo if needed. The session window shows HP/FP and history.

6. Keep result and Compare do not change the session. History retains up to 20 outputs per tool during this run. Export a result to keep it permanently.

Language and units are independent. Previous results retain their original text without new rolls. Ctrl+H opens Home; View provides theme, font size and collapsible navigation.

qt_scamp_requires_mass: Mass Combat, with the two forces and their battle context already determined.
qt_scamp_requires_class: One applicable class at a time; first total the adjusted TS of relevant elements.
qt_scamp_requires_strategy: Base strategy reference; it does not validate initiative, surprise, terrain or the opponent's choice.
qt_scamp_requires_risk: Individual risk for one round; Heroism is for PCs who are not commanding the force.
qt_scamp_requires_aftermath: Use after determining the winner and withdrawal conditions; nothing is applied to the campaign.
qt_scamp_requires_fright: Horror options for a scene the GM considers frightening. Size is perceived size, not SM.
qt_scamp_requires_fear: Optional cumulative fear rule; confirm with the GM before using.
qt_scamp_requires_stress: Optional Stress and Derangement model, separate from simple cumulative fear.
qt_scamp_reaction_bands: ≤0 disastrous; 1–3 very bad; 4–6 bad; 7–9 poor; 10–12 neutral; 13–15 good; 16–18 very good; ≥19 excellent.
qt_scamp_reaction_reference: Check the consequence and exceptions for {context}, p. {page}. These bands are not success rolls.
qt_scamp_rank_target: AR 9 at Rank {rank}; base {base}, prior requests {repeated}, other {modifier} → AR {target}.
qt_scamp_rank_blocked: Final AR below 3: do not roll or count it as a prior request.
qt_scamp_rank_aid: Standard outcome: the organization provides the requested aid.
qt_scamp_rank_no_aid: Standard outcome: no aid. If the request was inappropriate, check disciplinary consequences on p. 11.
qt_scamp_rank_guide: Count only requests that were rolled. For guaranteed, secret or capricious aid, check the exceptions before using the standard outcome.
qt_scamp_strength_required: Enter positive TS for both fighting forces.
qt_scamp_strength_result: Larger:smaller ratio ≈ {odds}:1. Strategy bonus: A +{a}; B +{b}.
qt_scamp_strength_guide: Use TS adjusted for terrain and conditions. For total TS, parenthetical support TS counts at 10% (zero if C3I is its only class).
qt_scamp_opposing_ts: Total TS of the enemy facing the stronger side in this class
qt_scamp_class_totals: Class TS after neutralization: A {a}; B {b}.
qt_scamp_class_none: No bonus: neither side has an edge in this class.
qt_scamp_class_opposing_required: Enter side {side}'s total TS to check the 1% minimum.
qt_scamp_class_insignificant: No bonus: class TS is less than 1% of total enemy TS.
qt_scamp_class_recon_result: {cls} bonus in the Reconnaissance Contest: A +{a}; B +{b}.
qt_scamp_class_guide: Include full support TS in this class. Check applicability to terrain and battle type (especially Engineering and Naval). Do not count a neutralizing element twice.
qt_scamp_length_result: The smaller side has {count} elements: {minutes} min per round.
qt_scamp_length_guide: Use the element count, not Troop Strength (TS). Reassess modifiers if the battle shifts from day to night.
qt_scamp_casualty_gap: Own casualties minus enemy casualties (percentage points)
qt_scamp_strategy_desperate_invalid: This strategy does not allow the Desperate option.
qt_scamp_strategy_desperate_minimum: The {gap}-point gap is below the required 25 percentage points.
qt_scamp_strategy_desperate_result: With Desperate: {total} to Strategy before other adjustments; +10 percentage points of own losses and +1 to Misfortunes of War.
qt_scamp_strategy_guide: Check eligibility, superiority and the strategy's effects before resolving the Quick Contest of Strategy.
qt_scamp_guide_all_out_attack: On a win, inflict 5 extra percentage points of casualties; double own losses.
qt_scamp_guide_all_out_defense: Reduce PB loss by 1, but double own losses.
qt_scamp_guide_attack: Standard attack with no special effects.
qt_scamp_guide_defense: Can use Defense Bonus (DB), but cannot gain Position Bonus (PB).
qt_scamp_guide_deliberate_attack: Halve the opponent's DB (round up), yield initiative and check for an Artillery bonus.
qt_scamp_guide_deliberate_defense: Inflict 5 extra percentage points on a win or tie, yield initiative, and check for a Fire bonus.
qt_scamp_guide_fighting_retreat: Escape on a win or tie. Halve casualties inflicted on the enemy; check logistics losses and PB if defeated.
qt_scamp_guide_full_retreat: Escape with survivors; inflict no losses and reduce own losses by 10 percentage points. Check logistics, confusion and terrain.
qt_scamp_guide_indirect_attack: May double the winning margin; check repeated attempts and C3I.
qt_scamp_guide_mobile_defense: Fewer own losses (−5 percentage points), but the enemy gets an extra +1 PB; check mobility requirements.
qt_scamp_guide_parley: Yield initiative. If refused, treat it as Defense with an extra −1 penalty.
qt_scamp_guide_raid: On a win, may reduce enemy PB or cause logistics losses; does not gain PB.
qt_scamp_guide_rally: A confused force can roll Leadership at −2 to end confusion (see context on pp. 34–35).
qt_scamp_guide_skirmish: Halve the winning margin; gain no PB; reduce own losses by 5 percentage points.
qt_scamp_battle_tie: Tie: {percent}% casualties on each side, no PB shift from the table.
qt_scamp_battle_shift: PB shift: +{shift} in the winner's favor. Reduce enemy PB first.
qt_scamp_battle_raid: Raid can remove up to {shift} enemy PB without awarding PB to the winner.
qt_scamp_battle_no_shift: This category does not receive the winner's PB shift from the table.
qt_scamp_battle_base: Apply strategy effects separately. Add casualties to the running total; each 5% accumulated gives −1 to the Basic Strategy Modifier. Do not reduce TS during battle.
qt_scamp_desperate: Your side used a Desperate strategy (Misfortunes only)
qt_scamp_useful: Useful skill at 15+ or especially useful resource (Heroism only)
qt_scamp_unit_leader: Commanding or second-in-command of an element (Heroism only)
qt_scamp_support: Logistics, or support with more than one fighting element
qt_scamp_risk_unlisted: {loss}% is not in the Misfortunes table (first entry: 5%). Check with the GM.
qt_scamp_risk_too_low: Final target below 3. Check with the GM whether a roll applies.
qt_scamp_risk_heroism_result: Significant action: {bonus} to the commander's Strategy this round.
qt_scamp_risk_bad: Misfortune: 2d−1 HP of injury, not damage (do not apply DR).
qt_scamp_risk_bad_critical: Critical misfortune: choose surrender or 6d HP of injury before rolling.
qt_scamp_risk_intact: No injury from Misfortunes of War.
qt_scamp_risk_guide: Commanders also add their own Risk to Strategy. The GM decides immunity and narrative consequences.
qt_scamp_after_title: After the battle: pursuit and final casualties
qt_scamp_after_mutual: Mutual annihilation: apply winner recovery to both sides.
qt_scamp_after_no_winner: The supposed winner alone has taken 100% casualties. Check which side won.
qt_scamp_after_not_retreat: The action requires voluntary withdrawal by the losing side with survivors.
qt_scamp_after_pursuit: Pursuit: +{increase} percentage points of enemy losses; if using a logistic force, roll 1d × 5% for its losses.
qt_scamp_after_holding: Holding the field reduces the winner's losses by 5 percentage points before recovery.
qt_scamp_after_final: Final casualties: designated winner {winner}%; designated loser {loser}%.
qt_scamp_after_guide: After withdrawal, Leadership allows choosing the action; without success (or without rolling), 1d decides: 1–3 pursue, 4–6 hold. Winner recovery halves its casualties and rounds down to a multiple of 5%.
qt_scamp_fright_limit: Standard check (Rule of 14): effective target {target}, at most 13.
qt_scamp_fright_scene_guide: Other factors are situational: familiarity, perceived threat and darkness. For bodies, use p. 140 (number, proximity and relationship) rather than monster adjustments when appropriate.
qt_scamp_fright_too_low: Effective target below 3. Confirm with the GM how to handle the check and margin.
qt_scamp_fright_table_check: If using the standard table, add the failure margin ({margin}) to a fresh 3d roll and consult B360–361. The GM may choose a different consequence.
qt_scamp_fright_ad_hoc: With the group's agreement, the GM can assign 1d seconds of stun now. The actual Fright Check and its consequences can wait until after the action (p. 139).
qt_scamp_fright_alternatives: If the result would be stun, consider a harsher result from the table, flight or frenzy after the first second, or actions of no tactical value. Confirm with the GM; p. 141.
qt_scamp_fear_cumulative_guide: A failure increases fear by 1; a success recovers 1 without granting a bonus. The penalty usually lasts one adventure. Do not automatically stack modifiers from threats revealed in stages.
qt_scamp_blast: It was a Sanity-Blasting Fright Check
qt_scamp_stress_limits: Each track can only be up to {limit} before the check. First convert excess Stress to Derangement, and excess Derangement to disadvantage points.
qt_scamp_stress_result: After the event: Stress {stress}; Derangement {deranged}; Fright Check penalty {penalty}; new permanent disadvantage points {permanent}.
qt_scamp_stress_guide: Ordinary failures add Stress; Sanity-Blasting failures add Derangement. Critical failure adds 3 instead of 1. Each track recovers differently (p. 142); nothing is applied to the character sheet.
qt_hazard_damage_scope: Preview for a normal living target: a single torso hit, rigid DR and no armor divisor. Armor degradation and special effects are not tracked.
qt_hazard_damage_shock: Shock: {modifier} to DX, IQ and skills based on them on the next turn; no penalty to active defenses.
qt_hazard_damage_major: Major Wound: roll against HT to avoid knockdown and stunning.
qt_hazard_invalid_vitals: Current HP and FP cannot exceed their maximum. FP cannot be below the negative of its maximum.
qt_hazard_vitals_low_hp: Below one-third HP: halve Move and Dodge, rounding up.
qt_hazard_vitals_collapse: To stay awake when acting or defending, roll HT each turn with modifier {modifier}. No roll if you Do Nothing and do not defend.
qt_hazard_vitals_death_rolls: Roll against HT immediately when injury crosses {first}, {second}, {third} or {fourth} HP. Failure by 1–2 is a Mortal Wound; a worse failure is fatal.
qt_hazard_vitals_low_fp: Below one-third FP: halve Move, Dodge and ST, rounding up. HP and damage based on ST are unchanged.
qt_hazard_vitals_spillover: Below zero FP, each additional point of fatigue also costs 1 HP. At the FP floor, additional fatigue costs HP instead.
qt_hazard_vitals_will: At 0 FP or lower, roll Will before attempting more than talking or resting. Failure leaves you incapacitated until FP is positive.
qt_hazard_vitals_fp_unconscious: At the negative of maximum FP: unconscious until FP is positive.
qt_hazard_vitals_dead: Automatic death at {limit} HP or lower.
qt_hazard_vitals_destroyed: The body can be destroyed at {limit} HP or lower, depending on the source of injury.
qt_hazard_vitals_no_thresholds: No low-HP or low-FP threshold has been reached.
qt_hazard_aid_bandage: Bandaging takes 1 minute and restores up to {amount} HP.
qt_hazard_aid_treatment: Treating Shock: {time} minutes per patient; on success roll {expression} for {minimum}–{maximum} HP total, including bandaging.
qt_hazard_aid_critical: A critical success restores up to {maximum} HP; a critical failure costs 2 HP instead of healing.
qt_hazard_aid_optional_bleeding: If using the optional Bleeding rule, successful First Aid within a minute prevents the first loss; later success stops further bleeding.
qt_hazard_aid_high_hp: High HP and Healing: multiply HP restored by {multiplier}.
qt_hazard_aid_success_roll: Healing die {roll}: up to {total} HP total if the skill roll succeeded, of which up to {extra} HP is in addition to bandaging.
qt_hazard_bleed_optional: Optional rule: the GM decides which wounds bleed. Check once per minute after wounding.
qt_hazard_bleed_check: HT modifier {modifier}, giving a target number of {target}.
qt_hazard_bleed_prior_stop: Three consecutive minutes without blood loss: bleeding stops.
qt_hazard_bleed_outcomes: Failure costs 1 HP; critical failure costs 3 HP. Critical success or three consecutive minutes without blood loss ends bleeding.
qt_hazard_bleed_stop: Critical success: bleeding stops; no HP loss.
qt_hazard_bleed_hit: Bleeding costs {amount} HP; restart the count of minutes without loss.
qt_hazard_bleed_continue: No HP loss this minute ({successes}/3 consecutive); check again in a minute.
qt_hazard_fire_partial_turn: Part of a turn in fire
qt_hazard_fire_full_turn: Full turn in ordinary fire or already burning
qt_hazard_fire_damage: Basic burning damage from one hit (optional)
qt_hazard_fire_partial_turn_result: Part of a turn in the fire: 1d−3 burning damage.
qt_hazard_fire_full_turn_result: A full turn in ordinary fire: 1d−1 burning damage per second.
qt_hazard_fire_intense_result: Example for a furnace or molten metal: 3d burning damage per second.
qt_hazard_fire_large_area: Resolve exposure as Large-Area Injury. These are damage expressions, not injury or HP loss after DR.
qt_hazard_fire_clothing_scope: Ordinary dry outer clothing: {damage} Basic Damage for the ignition check (tight-beam burning damage counts at one-tenth).
qt_hazard_fire_full_clothes: All clothing catches fire: 1d−1 burning damage per second and −3 DX, except on the roll to put out the fire.
qt_hazard_fire_partial_clothes: Part of the clothing catches fire: 1d−4 burning damage per second. Apply −2 DX if the fire can injure the target.
qt_hazard_fire_no_clothes: This hit does not ignite ordinary clothing. Special materials or prolonged exposure may differ.
qt_hazard_airless_seconds: Seconds with no air after holding your breath
qt_hazard_airless_scope: Complete lack of air only: 1 FP per second. Drowning with some air uses Swimming instead.
qt_hazard_airless_result: Projected remaining FP: {fp}. Accumulated HP loss due to fatigue spillover: {damage}, before checks or rescue.
qt_hazard_airless_death: After four minutes without air, death is automatic regardless of remaining HP or FP.
qt_hazard_airless_unconscious: Unconscious on reaching the FP floor. If rescued, recover consciousness at 1 FP.
qt_hazard_airless_will: At 0 FP or less, roll Will each second to avoid losing consciousness.
qt_hazard_airless_brain: After more than two minutes without air, a survivor must roll HT to avoid permanent −1 IQ.
qt_hazard_rad_result: Dose after shielding: {dose} rads; today: {remaining}, of which {permanent} do not heal naturally. Accumulated total: {accumulated} rads.
qt_hazard_rad_scope: Each dose heals separately after 30 days. Use the band below only when a new radiation check is due; repeated exposure to one source allows no more than one check a day.
qt_hazard_rad_below_table: Accumulated dose below 1 rad: no row in the Radiation Effects Table.
qt_hazard_rad_ambiguous: At exactly 800 rads the printed ranges overlap. The GM chooses between HT−4 (A/B/C/D) and HT−5 (C/D/E/E).
qt_hazard_rad_band: If a radiation check is due: HT {modifier}. Effect codes by critical success / success / failure / critical failure: {effects}. Consult p. 436 for symptoms and timing.
qt_hazard_cold_guide: In ordinary freezing weather roll against the better of HT or HT-based Survival (Arctic) each 30 min. Use 15 min at 10+ mph (≈16 km/h), or 10 min at 30+ mph (≈48 km/h). Failure costs 1 FP. Account for clothing, wind chill, immersion and Temperature Tolerance separately.
qt_hazard_heat_guide: When active in the upper 10°F of your comfort zone or above it (normally over 80°F, ≈27°C), check the better of HT or HT-based Survival (Desert) every 30 min. Account for encumbrance and additional heat. Failure costs 1 FP, critical failure 1d FP; intense heat and exertion require their own checks.
qt_hazard_electricity_guide: Nonlethal shock usually requires a modified HT roll against stun. For lethal shock, determine burning injury first: if any gets through, roll HT at −1 per 2 HP of injury. Check localized exposure and any special weapon rules before applying severe effects.
qt_hazard_poison_guide: Identify delivery, delay, dose and cycle first. If resistance is allowed, use the toxin’s HT modifier after its delay; DR is not a bonus to a poison resistance roll. Exposure and repeated checks depend on the agent. No universal damage or duration applies.
qt_hazard_falls_guide: Use the Falls calculator for height, impact speed, surface and protection. Controlled falls, water entry and hit location require their specific rules.
qt_hazard_collisions_guide: Use the Collisions calculator for impact with moving or stationary objects. Check relative speed, impact angle and protection for the chosen case.
qt_hazard_explosions_guide: Use the Explosions calculator for blast and fragmentation. Direct hits and collateral effects do not use the same DR and distance rules; consider the environment too.

psi_effect_emotion_sense: The GM reveals the emotional state sensed.
psi_effect_mental_surgery: The GM confirms the change to mental disadvantages; the sheet is not edited automatically.
vehicle_combat_too_many_dice: This collision exceeds the 100,000-die limit for synchronous vehicle rolls.
encounter_unknown_defenses: Defenses not calculated in this sheet: {values}.
encounter_defense_required: The sheet doesn't provide {defense}. Enter the effective defense for this attack.
encounter_ranged_dodge_missing: The target's sheet doesn't provide Dodge. Check the defense in the Ranged tab before resolving.

encounter_ranged_sm_missing: The sheet doesn't provide effective SM. The manual Ranged value was retained.

encounter_invalid_resource: Check the resource name, limit, and current value.
encounter_roster_limit: The roster can hold up to 100 participants.
encounter_minimum_roster: Keep at least two participants in the scenario to select an actor and a target.
encounter_invalid_edit: This change is not valid for the current scenario.
encounter_invalid_order: The selected position is not in this roster.
encounter_duplicate_combatant: A participant with this identifier already exists.
encounter_insufficient_resource: The pool does not have enough points for this action.
qt_prep_hp_guide: Prefer listed HP when available. Do not infer DR from weight; the GM may adjust HP for unusual construction.
qt_prep_material_guide: The GM picks a value within the range for the actual barrier. This is cover DR, not the object's own DR or HP; do not add it again to another cover DR estimate.
qt_prep_material_wear: Repeated hits on the same small spot can wear down cover DR. Track this separately by damage type (p. 559).
qt_prep_cover_title: Cover from known DR and HP
qt_prep_slab: Thin slab (e.g., a wall or door)
qt_prep_cover_result: Cover DR: {total} ({dr} intrinsic DR + {hp} from HP).
qt_prep_cover_guide: For eligible overpenetration; the estimate is before the attack's armor divisor and before any armor on the next target. Check the path and material with the GM.
qt_prep_mover_hp: Full HP of the moving object
qt_prep_collision_none: Impact speed is zero; there is no collision damage.
qt_prep_collision_dice: Crushing damage before any cap or DR: moving object takes {incoming}; obstacle takes {outgoing}.
qt_prep_collision_cap: Cap against either side after rolling: {cap} (obstacle HP + DR).
qt_prep_collision_elastic: Apply {dr} extra DR against damage to the moving object.
qt_prep_collision_guide: Preview only. For moving targets, a dive or ditching, occupant effects, or a damage roll, use the appropriate vehicle or collision rules.
qt_prep_vehicle_location: Eligible location chosen for this result and attack angle
qt_prep_no_candidate: Confirmed: no listed candidate is eligible
qt_prep_vehicle_guide: Check the vehicle's location codes, whether the part is exposed, and the attack angle. If more than one candidate is eligible, the attacker chooses; if none are eligible, the hit is on the body. Evaluate occupants separately (p. 555).
qt_prep_vehicle_pending: Roll {roll}: no eligible location has been confirmed for this result.
qt_prep_vehicle_penalty: Location modifier for deliberately aiming at this part: {penalty:+d}, before vehicle SM. Do not apply to this random hit.
qt_prep_vehicle_animal: For a deliberate attack, use the draft animal's own SM instead of the vehicle's location modifier.
qt_prep_magic_title: Mana, skill, energy and casting time
qt_prep_base_skill: Base spell skill (before mana and other modifiers)
qt_prep_spell_kind: Spell class (for cost and time exceptions)
qt_prep_spell_cost: Casting energy (after area and SM; before skill reduction)
qt_prep_spell_seconds: Listed casting time (seconds; ignored for Blocking)
qt_prep_magic_no_mana: No mana: standard magic does not function here.
qt_prep_magic_need_magery: Standard magic requires Magery in low or normal mana.
qt_prep_magic_skill: Skill used for ritual, time and energy: {skill} (mana modifier {mod:+d}).
qt_prep_magic_effect: Casting: {cost} energy; skill reduction {reduction}; {seconds} s (0 means instant).
qt_prep_ritual_large: free hands and feet for a full ritual, plus audible words
qt_prep_ritual_words_or_gesture: brief words or a small gesture
qt_prep_magic_very_high: Very high mana: ordinary casting failures become critical; a naturally critical failure can be worse at the GM's discretion.
qt_prep_magic_very_high_recovery: A mage recovers FP spent on casting at the start of the next turn.
qt_prep_magic_low_effect: In low mana, critical failures may be minor or have no effect, at the GM's discretion.
qt_prep_magic_guide: For ordinary individual casting only. A spell's specific minimum energy and ritual override this quick estimate. Handle ceremonial casting, charging a missile, and resistance in their own procedures.
qt_prep_spell_distance: Distance to subject or nearest edge
qt_prep_touch: Caster can touch the subject or area
qt_prep_see: Caster can see the subject or area
qt_prep_spell_range_long_guide: Use only when the spell or trait specifies long-distance modifiers. The ordinary touch and sight fields do not apply to this lookup.
qt_prep_spell_range_guide_regular: Measure to the subject at the moment of casting. Touch removes these range and sight penalties.
qt_prep_spell_range_guide_area: Measure to the nearest edge; radius sets energy cost, not this range penalty. Touching any part of the area removes these range and sight penalties.
qt_prep_effective_skill: Effective skill (includes mana and all modifiers)
qt_prep_spell_minimum_skill: Effective skill below 3: an ordinary casting roll is not allowed.
qt_prep_spell_backfire_reference: For a standard backfire, consult Critical Spell Failure (p. 236), or have the GM choose an appropriate effect. This result does not apply an effect or spend energy.
qt_prep_spell_check_guide: This is an ordinary casting check. Use the spell-specific procedure for Information spells, ceremonial magic, resistance, and spells with special failure rules.
qt_prep_wealth_title: Starting wealth and cost of living
qt_prep_settled: Apply the 80/20 split for a settled lifestyle
qt_prep_status: Status used to pay cost of living
qt_prep_wealth_result: Typical starting wealth for this TL: ${base}; after Wealth level: ${starting}.
qt_prep_wealth_split: Movable possessions or cash: ${movable}; already tied up in the household: ${settled}.
qt_prep_status_result: Generic monthly cost of living at the chosen Status: ${monthly}.
qt_prep_wealth_guide: Amounts are generic GURPS dollars, not historical exchange rates. Use the setting's prices and the appropriate paid Status (e.g., account for Rank where applicable).
qt_prep_encounter_slot: Use entry {slot} of your own six-entry table.
qt_prep_encounter_guide: Prepare six original entries appropriate to the region and situation. Decide whether and when an encounter occurs separately. Use this roll only to pick an entry; give it a reason to be there and change or skip it if it would disrupt play.
qt_prep_artifact_title: Damage thresholds for an object or building
qt_prep_artifact_stressed: Artifact is in use or under stress
qt_prep_artifact_collapse: Automatic collapse at or below −5× full HP.
qt_prep_artifact_destroyed: Automatically destroyed at or below −5× full HP.
qt_prep_artifact_collapse_check: Check HT when crossing collapse thresholds from −1× full HP onward. Do not repeat an already resolved threshold.
qt_prep_artifact_destruction_check: Check HT when crossing destruction thresholds from −1× full HP onward. Do not repeat an already resolved threshold.
qt_prep_artifact_building_disable_check: Check HT for disabling damage; failure can cause serious breaches and loss of power.
qt_prep_artifact_stress_check: Check HT every second while under stress; failure disables the artifact.
qt_prep_artifact_wait_for_stress: At 0 HP or below, ordinary artifacts check HT every second only while under stress.
qt_prep_artifact_impaired: Less than one-third of full HP: the GM may reduce its effectiveness.
qt_prep_artifact_above_thresholds: This HP total does not cross a general impairment or destruction threshold.
qt_prep_artifact_guide: This lookup does not track past checks, local crippling, Fragile effects, or special breakage and repair (pp. 484–485).
qt_ssuper_black_req: Use only when casting with demonic assistance. This table follows any failed casting, not just a critical failure.
qt_ssuper_black_not_applicable: Confirm a failed demon-assisted casting before using this table.
qt_ssuper_black_pending: Roll an independent 3d for the GM or enter the total.
qt_ssuper_black_ref: Total {roll}: consult the Black Critical Table (p. 157). Adapt the outcome to the spell and setting; nothing is applied automatically.
qt_ssuper_calamity_req: Use only for a campaign using Threshold-Limited Magic; this lookup uses the ordinary step of five tally points.
qt_ssuper_casting: Cast a spell (even at zero tally cost)
qt_ssuper_maintenance: Add tally to maintain a spell
qt_ssuper_calamity_not_applicable: This event does not require a Calamity Check: you did not go over the threshold, or you were already over it without casting or adding maintenance tally.
qt_ssuper_calamity_modifier: Tally exceeds the threshold by {excess}; roll 3d with a {mod:+d} modifier.
qt_ssuper_calamity_ref: Roll {roll}; adjusted total {total}. Consult the campaign's Calamity Table (suggested table on pp. 77–78).
qt_ssuper_calamity_casting_will: At 29+, the spell fails unless the caster makes a Will roll at {mod:+d}.
qt_ssuper_calamity_guide: Optional advantages, altered thresholds, and specific consequences require separate GM adjudication. This does not change tally or resolve a spell.
qt_ssuper_rpm_title: Ritual Path Magic: estimate ritual energy
qt_ssuper_rpm_req: Use the Ritual Path Magic system, not ordinary skill-based magic. The GM determines which effects and modifiers apply.
qt_ssuper_rpm_subject_weight: Weight of largest eligible subject (blank if inapplicable)
qt_ssuper_rpm_other_energy: Other effects and modifiers, including special/long durations
qt_ssuper_rpm_greater_count: Total Greater effects in the ritual
qt_ssuper_rpm_breakdown: Energy: first effect {effect}; duration {duration}; weight {weight}; manually entered {other}.
qt_ssuper_rpm_total: Subtotal {subtotal} × {multiplier} for Greater effects = {total} energy before any discounts.
qt_ssuper_rpm_guide: Do not charge for weight on purely mental effects. Damage and healing do not use the ordinary Duration modifier. Add other modifiers in their own field without counting duration or weight twice. This does not model accumulation or discounts.
qt_ssuper_lift_req: Use only with Lifting ST that has the Super-Effort enhancement from Powers. This is not the Supers variant for Striking ST or total ST.
qt_ssuper_lift_base_st: ST before the enhanced Lifting ST levels
qt_ssuper_lift_scores: Normal lifting ST: {normal}. With Super-Effort: {boosted} (enhanced levels become +{bonus}); {cost} FP for one lift.
qt_ssuper_lift_guide: Continuing to carry or pull costs 1 FP/minute; holding alone costs 1 FP/hour. The enhancement does not boost grapples or chokes.
qt_ssuper_awe_title: Consequence of failed Awe or Confusion
qt_ssuper_awe_req: Only for a failed Awe or Confusion Check using the Powers variants (not an ordinary Fright Check).
qt_ssuper_awe_need_failure: Enter the margin of the failed {mode} Check first.
qt_ssuper_awe_need_roll: {mode} Check failed by {margin}. Roll a new 3d for the consequence or enter the total.
qt_ssuper_awe_ref: {mode}: {roll} + {margin} = {total}. Consult the corresponding result in the table (p. 85); many entries differ between the two effects.
qt_ssuper_psi_range_req: Use only if the ability specifies the Psionic Range Table; some abilities adjust their actual level for this lookup.
qt_ssuper_psi_offset: Level adjustment stated by the ability
qt_ssuper_psi_bad_level: Adjusted level {level} is below 1; this table does not give a range for it.
qt_ssuper_psi_range_scope: At adjusted level {level}, the table gives at least {scope} range.
qt_ssuper_psi_cripple_req: The GM must have chosen Optional Crippling Rules and confirmed that the ability or power is actually crippled; an ordinary failed psi roll is not enough.
qt_ssuper_psi_cripple_confirmed: Confirm ongoing crippling under the optional rule
qt_ssuper_psi_cripple_not_applicable: First confirm the optional rule is active and this ability or power has been crippled.
qt_ssuper_psi_cripple_pending: Roll 3d in secret as the GM, or enter a total you already rolled.
qt_ssuper_psi_cripple_ref: GM only: consult result {roll} under Optional Crippling Rules (p. 7). Resolve any additional choices or rolls privately; do not expose this result to the affected player.
qt_ssuper_solar_req: Use the rounded game data in Spaceships, not as current real-world ephemerides or a route calculation.
qt_ssuper_solar_radius: Nominal orbital distance from the Sun: {radius:g} AU.
qt_ssuper_solar_luna: The Moon's distance shown here is heliocentric; the table does not give its lunar orbital speed or period.
qt_ssuper_solar_oort: For this example, use negligible surface gravity and escape velocity.
qt_ssuper_solar_guide: Choose the route distance separately. Two bodies' listed orbital radii do not determine their current separation.
qt_ssuper_voyage_req: For free flight with a reactionless drive and fixed acceleration. This is not for reaction-drive fuel budgeting, orbit departure, atmospheric flight, or FTL.
qt_ssuper_voyage_long: For {distance:g} AU, estimated time is {hours:.5g} hours ({days:.5g} days).
qt_ssuper_voyage_guide: The equations already include acceleration and braking for the selected distance. Excludes any time to leave orbit or land.
qt_ssuper_voyage_relativistic: The estimated speed is at least one tenth of light speed. Treat this Newtonian estimate cautiously and consult the high-speed rules.
qt_ssuper_voyage_out_of_model: This Newtonian estimate would reach or exceed light speed. Use the high-speed travel rules instead (pp. 39–40).
qt_ssuper_sensor_req: Use the comm/sensor array's level, not an operator's skill or the spacecraft's Size Modifier.
qt_ssuper_sensor_range: Level {level}: active sensor {light_seconds:g} light-seconds (book approximation: {approx}); communications {au:g} AU.
qt_ssuper_sensor_guide: Active sensor and communications values use different units; this is not a passive detection roll or a targeting bonus.
qt_ssuper_combat_range_req: Use the abstract combat scales from Spaceships, not the Basic Set distance penalties in yards.
qt_ssuper_combat_range_guide: Confirm which maneuver and formation still apply on this turn. The result is a category, not a physical distance or a resolved attack.
map_need_pair: Place the actor and target on the map to measure.
map_settings_stale: The map changed. Reopen grid settings or measure again.
map_background_missing: The background is unavailable. Grid and tokens were preserved.
map_help: Drag tokens to move them. Use the wheel to zoom and the middle button to pan. New tokens start hidden; use “Visible to players” before or after placing them.
battle_map_image_too_large: The PNG exceeds the map size limit.
battle_map_image_invalid: The file is not a valid PNG.
battle_map_image_invalid_id: The local background reference is invalid.
battle_map_image_write_failed: Could not save the image in the data folder.
ranged_map_distance_stale: The map measurement is out of date. To calculate or roll, send a new distance or edit the field manually.
quick_tables_intro: Look up rules and prepare rolls without changing the current encounter.
qt_sfant_wilderness_context: Use Dungeon Fantasy's detailed travel and foraging rules instead of the simplified Basic reference.
qt_sfant_treasure_context: Applies to Dungeon Fantasy's economy and treasure tables.
qt_sfant_low_hp_or_fp: HP or FP below 1/3 from lasting losses
qt_sfant_stops_beyond_hours: Stops exceed the time available for travel.
qt_sfant_travel_adjusted: Move after health adjustment: {move}. Hours of travel: {hours}.
qt_sfant_travel_group: Use the transport multiplier when it replaces the terrain. Add weather, tracking, and other applicable adjustments; calculate each member and take the slowest.
qt_sfant_travel_negative: A negative result means the group lost ground, such as by backtracking.
qt_sfant_forage_skill: Gathering, Fishing, hunting, or trapping skill
qt_sfant_forage_scope: For foraging instead of travel. The GM confirms available food and water and the appropriate method.
qt_sfant_forage_no_test: Effective skill is below 3: do not attempt the roll.
qt_sfant_forage_harm: Critical failure: no meal and 1 HP lost; the GM decides the cause.
qt_sfant_forage_spear_harm: Critical failure when hunting up close: no meal and 1d6 HP lost.
qt_sfant_forage_ammo: Account for ammunition spent or the retrieval of the thrown weapon. Nothing was spent in the session.
qt_sfant_cost_scope: Add the factors before multiplying. Then add allowed flat-cost embellishments and enchantments.
qt_sfant_cost_floor: The total was below −0.8, so the supplement's floor was applied.
qt_sfant_town_weeks: Paid weeks in town per person
qt_sfant_days_away: Days of rations away from town per person
qt_sfant_budget_scope: Include lighting, consumables, training, or discounts as appropriate. This is not a mandatory reward value.
qt_sfant_ordered_dice_guide: Read the three individual dice in order in Dice. Ignore their sum: each die is a column in the book's table key.
qt_reference_out_of_range: The value is outside the reference's limits.
quick_tables_dimming: Sudden dimming: levels of light lost
quick_tables_total_darkness_notice: If the target cannot be seen, consider “{setting}” and handle random hit location separately (Basic Set Revised, p. 394).
quick_tables_map_used: Distance copied from the map for the current actor and target.
quick_tables_map_stale: The map measurement is out of date. Read it again or enter a distance manually.
quick_tables_sense_no_send: Sense modifiers are not used for ranged attacks.
quick_tables_invalid_option: Choose a valid option for this table.
quick_tables_invalid_range: Check the distance and target speed.
